display.title: Pirkei Avos: Humility from Har Sinai and the Unity of Matan Torah
display.summary_short: Good character comes before Torah: why we learn Pirkei Avos before Shavuos, what Moshe learned from the lowest mountain, and how the Jews camped at Sinai as one person with one heart.
display.summary_long: A short Sefirah-time talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi explains the saying 'derech eretz kodmah laTorah': even though learning Torah outweighs all other mitzvos, good character comes first, because the Torah is meant to refine our midos. That is why, between Pesach (leaving Egypt) and Shavuos (receiving the Torah), we prepare by learning a chapter of Pirkei Avos each Shabbos. The very first Mishnah teaches humility: Moshe received the Torah 'from Sinai', learning from the mountain itself, which Hashem chose because it was the lowest. To serve Hashem truly we must be humble and see the good qualities in others, which leads to Ahavas Yisroel and unity. At Har Sinai the Torah says 'he camped' in the singular, because the Jewish people were like one person with one heart, and in the merit of such unity Moshiach will gather us all back to Eretz Yisroel.
display.lesson: Work on good character before Shavuos: be humble, see the good in others, and stay united.
